Package hadur117.core.policy

Class EnergyRace

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.policy.EnergyRace
public final class EnergyRace extends Object
POW-17: bullet power chosen by the rest of the round's energy race, for the opponents the mode table names (race-power:).

The other power rules each look at one thing: a tier, a range, a rate, a lead. This one values a power by what it does to the whole remaining exchange. The round from here is a race between two energies: each side fires at the rate its gun heat allows, each shot costs its power, a hit takes the bullet's damage from the target and gives the shooter three times the power back. The value of a pair of energies is the expected score still to come, ours less theirs: the bullet damage each side still deals, and ROUND_SWING for the side left alive (survival, the last-survivor bonus and roughly the kill bonus). We fire whichever power gives the highest value; the opponent fires the power it has been firing, capped by its energy.

The values are solved on a grid of energy pairs, finer at low energy where single shots decide rounds, by value iteration with bilinear interpolation between grid points. A shot moves the energies by less than a grid cell, so most of a state's successors interpolate back onto the state itself; that share is solved in closed form per power, which is what lets a few sweeps converge. Hit chances come from this battle's own counts with a prior, and are moved to other powers by the ratio of maximum escape angles: a slower bullet gives the target a wider arc to be in. Range, walls, ramming and bullet shadows are not modelled.

The solve is spread over the calls, ROWS_PER_CALL grid rows each. Until both sides have MIN_SHOTS resolved shots and WARMUP_SWEEPS sweeps are done, choose(double, double) returns NaN and the other rules stand. Bounded: a fixed grid, six counters, no allocation per tick (RES-2).
